answer: A licensed hand-paper mill anchors each identity: the miller dyes saffron-colored sheets, presses one pearl-white watermark page carrying that identity's sonnet, and files it with an independent paper guild. One operator cannot run two mills at once, and a mill takes weeks of real labor. The guild license fee in outside money doubles per mill on the same funding trail, so every extra fake identity costs another mill, another live miller, and twice the prior fee.
